title: gpu-node-memory-eviction-investigation-notes
summary: Notes from an on-call investigation into repeated pod evictions on GPU-backed nodes in us-west-2 between 2025-11-02 23:40 UTC and 2025-11-03 03:10 UTC. Root cause appears to be a GPU-resident memory leak in a newly rolled model-worker image combined with device-plugin/version skew that caused kubelet to treat node allocatable as reduced and schedule evictions.
incident_timeline:
2025-11-02 23:40 UTC: Alert fired: node-gpu-memory-usage > 90% for 3 nodes in gpu-pool-usw2
2025-11-02 23:43 UTC: On-call engineer (Tom) pulled k8s / monitoring dashboards and confirmed 3 nodes with high GPU memory but normal host RAM
2025-11-02 23:50 UTC: First application pod eviction observed on gpu-node-17 (pods using model-worker image v2.3.0)
2025-11-02 23:55 UTC: Cordon placed on gpu-node-17; non-critical batch jobs drained
2025-11-03 00:05 UTC: nvidia-smi on gpu-node-17 shows GPU memory 92% used, processes owned by container runtime (containerd)
2025-11-03 00:12 UTC: Restarted nvidia-device-plugin daemonset on gpu-node-17 and gpu-node-18; no immediate change
2025-11-03 00:25 UTC: Observed device-plugin logs showing: "failed to list devices: rpc error: code = Unavailable" on gpu-node-18 after a driver module update earlier in the week
2025-11-03 01:00 UTC: Rolled back model-worker from v2.3.0 -> v2.2.7 via rollout pause and image revert for the deployment used by latency-critical jobs
2025-11-03 01:28 UTC: GPU memory on gpu-node-17 gradually decreased as new pods scheduled off the node; evictions stopped by 03:10 UTC
2025-11-03 03:10 UTC: Incident declared contained; monitoring kept on for next 24h
detection_and_alerts: Primary alert: node-gpu-memory-usage > 90% for 10m (Prometheus rule). Secondary alert: kubelet-eviction-rate spike > 5 evictions/5m. Monitoring evidence: Grafana panels for GPU memory, node-exporter, device-plugin scrape targets; logs from datadog APM showing increased error rates for model-serving endpoints.
initial_symptoms:
- Application errors: increased 503/502 responses from model-serving endpoints.
- Pod evictions with message 'The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage' was NOT observed; evictions were attributed to 'memory' even though host memory was normal.
- Only nodes with GPUs were affected.
- No cluster-wide kubelet upgrades at the time of incident (checked release-engineering calendar).
impact:
- ~12 latency-critical requests failed per minute across two services during peak (est. 1.5% of user traffic for 30 minutes).
- Three GPU nodes had 20+ pods evicted and rescheduled onto non-GPU nodes, causing capacity contention.
- Temporary SLA degradation for model inference customers using dedicated GPU capacity.
- No data loss reported.
root_cause_hypothesis: Primary: A memory leak in the model-worker v2.3.0 image that allocates large GPU buffers per request and does not free them when container lifecycle events happen. Secondary contributing factor: NVIDIA device-plugin/driver version skew introduced earlier this week (driver v535 -> v536 on some nodes), causing intermittent device-plugin RPC failures and temporary allocatable reporting mismatch to kubelet, which triggered eviction heuristics for GPU-backed pods.
evidence:
- nvidia-smi snapshots showed persistent GPU memory held by PIDs that correspond to model-worker containers (containerd reported same PIDs).
- Device-plugin logs contained repeated 'failed to allocate device' and 'unavailable' grpc errors around 2025-11-02 23:40-00:20 UTC.
- No corresponding host OOM logs in kernel logs; system memory was stable.
- After rolling back model-worker to v2.2.7, average GPU memory per node decreased by 35% within 40 minutes.
- Jira ticket INF-2345 tracks a related change: model-worker introduced a caching layer in v2.3.0 that pins tensors to device across request contexts (design note in linked PR).
mitigation_actions_taken:
- Immediate: cordon and drain non-critical pods from affected nodes (Tom).
- Restarted nvidia-device-plugin daemonset on affected nodes (Lena).
- Rolled back model-worker images for latency-critical deployment to v2.2.7 (Marcus ran rollout undo).
- Increased autoscaler target for gpu-pool-usw2 to add two extra nodes for headroom.
- Pager duty: engaged model team to revert and provide hotfix.
long_term_actions:
- Enforce image-level canary policy for GPU workloads (stop wide rollout with more than 10% of GPU pool by default).
- Add GPU-memory usage alert per-namespace and per-deployment (not just per-node) to catch leaky workloads earlier.
- Add an end-to-end test that runs model-worker under load with nvidia-smi leak checks in CI before canary.
- Upgrade device-plugin to pinned version that matches tested driver (coordinate with infra to ensure uniform driver across gpu-pool).
- Add a lightweight watchdog sidecar for model-worker that monitors GPU allocations and restarts the container if long-lived allocations exceed threshold.
- Update capacity planner to reserve 10% buffer for GPU pool during nightly rollouts.
rollback_plan: If recurrence after fixes: immediate automatic rollback of any model-worker rollout to last known-good image and scale down new replicas to 0, cordon affected nodes, escalate to platform on-call. Documented steps: kubectl -n prod set image deployment/model-worker model-worker=redwood/model-worker:v2.2.7; kubectl rollout status; scale up autoscaler.
runbook_updates:
- Add a 'GPU node emergency' section: steps to collect nvidia-smi, containerd top, device-plugin logs, kubelet journal.
- Commands to run: 'kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=NODE', 'ssh NODE -- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 500', 'ssh NODE -- sudo docker ps -q | xargs -I{} sudo docker top {}', 'ssh NODE -- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY'.
- Add quick-restart steps for nvidia-device-plugin and guidance on when to restart kubelet vs. schedule node replacement.
- Add checklists for coordinating with infra (driver pins) and model team for canary limits.
postmortem_followups:
- INF-2345: model team to produce v2.3.1 hotfix that ensures tensors are explicitly freed and adds metrics for GPU allocations (owner: Marcus, due: 2025-11-10).
- INF-2346: infra to pin driver/device-plugin versions across gpu-pool (owner: Lena, due: 2025-11-12).
- Update autoscaler configuration to maintain 2 spare GPU nodes during business hours (owner: Aisha, due: 2025-11-15).
- Add CI job for GPU leak detection (owner: Tom, due: 2025-11-20).
notes_to_oncall:
- When you see GPU memory alerts: first confirm if PIDs correspond to expected workloads via container runtime mapping.
- Restarting the device-plugin is low-risk and often clears transient RPC errors; restart it before restarting kubelet except when driver mismatch is suspected.
- Use cordon+drain for affected node instead of immediate reboot unless kernel logs show driver panic.
- Keep the model team on the loop early; their image rollouts are primary suspect for GPU-only incidents.
- If rolling back an image, watch for reschedules that can spike CPU/host memory on non-GPU nodes.
